description:
Fetch one catalog product by UUID or slug with its AI-native scores
(``ai_native_score`` 0-100, ``ai_native_tier`` S/A/B/C/D) and related
organization, capabilities, and integrations (MCP servers, SDKs with languages
and licenses, CLIs, A2A servers, API specs, plugins) expanded inline as objects.
Also returned: a second research-coverage axis — ``coverage_score`` (0-100)
and the derived boolean ``unrated``. Coverage tells you how thoroughly the
product was researched before you trust the grade; ``unrated`` is true when
research coverage is too low to assign a letter grade (present as "Unrated /
needs research"). Plus the always-present ``attested_absences`` list — fields a
dated check attested absent (each a ``field_key`` or ``field_key:label`` for a
relation-scoped negative), the read booleans ``has_mcp``, ``has_mcp_url``,
``has_sdk``, ``has_api_spec``, ``has_cli``, ``has_a2a`` (each reads back its
filter), and ``free_plan`` (True for an active free-tier offer, else null;
never false).
``has_mcp_url`` is true when a cataloged MCP server has a dialable endpoint URL.
It is false when no MCP endpoint URL is cataloged.

``documented_task_completions`` contains all assessed jobs. Match each
selected job to ``job_to_be_done_slug`` or ``job_to_be_done_id``. Show its
``verdict``, ``scope``, and ``conditions`` with its assessment. The verdict
includes delegation limits. No matching record means
unassessed; a matching record with null ``completion_support`` means unknown.
Neither establishes inability to complete the job. Keep other jobs secondary.
If you use ``fields``, include ``documented_task_completions``.

The identifier is forwarded to the canonical ``{id-or-slug}`` detail route,
which owns the missing/ambiguous/invalid errors: an unknown value
is ``404``, a slug matching multiple products is ``409``, a malformed slug is
``400`` — each a structured tool error with the catalog's ``code`` and
``detail``, consistent with ``get_product_coverage``. ``fields`` trims the
payload; the default affordance relations are still expanded.

A missing or unknown value is JSON ``null`` on every field type — the
nullable booleans, the status enums (MFA, data-retention, sandbox,
portability), and the URL/text fields alike — so never read a blank as a
negative; the real negative is always explicit (``false``, or
``no``/``none``/``unavailable``). ``attested_absences`` then flags which
negatives are cited: listed is a cited "no", an explicit negative not listed
is recorded but uncited, and a ``null`` is unknown. The full attestation
records (``method``, ``source_url``, ``checked_at``) are not returned by
default; pass ``expand=absence_attestations`` to include them, and use
``expand`` to resolve any other relation ``*_ids`` into inline objects.

expand.description: Comma-separated product relations to expand inline beyond the affordance and documented_task_completions relations this tool always expands, following the REST ?expand= grammar. Example: compliance_certifications,offers,absence_attestations. Your values are added to the defaults, so name only the extras. An invalid value returns the allowed set.

fields.description: Comma-separated top-level response fields to include, following the REST ?fields= grammar. The response always keeps id. Narrows the payload for compact reads; an expanded relation is still returned only when its field is in the selection. Omit for the full record.

id.description: Alias for product, matching the REST {id-or-slug} route. Accepts a UUID or slug.

product_id.description: Legacy UUID-only argument. Use product instead.

name: get_product
title: Get Product
